- When sentiment is negative in the recent 3–5 days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate; apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is mixed (alternating +/–) — especially if recent sentiment is negative; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion in the final 7–10 days; apply a slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) in the last 7 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — increase forecast downward by 1–2% to reflect stronger bearish momentum.
